messages:
maria: heads up — we're seeing intermittent TLS handshake failures for requests to /inference/v2 in us-west-2. only on the dedicated pool behind the ALB. logs show client cert verify errors when traffic comes from our NAT egress subnets. not consistent across requests.

alex: ugh. any pattern on host header / SNI? ALB listener is TLS-terminating then reoriginate to backend TLS, right?

maria: yes TLS terminate -> TLS to backend. SNI in the backend connection sometimes empty per our nginx logs. reproducer attached below.

jun: can you paste the nginx reject log? also curious if proxy_protocol is on for the target group.

maria: nginx error: 
```
2026/03/18 14:02:12 [error] 23456#0: *1123 SSL_do_handshake() failed (SSL: error:1408F10B:SSL routines:ssl3_get_record:wrong version number) while SSL handshake, client: 10.0.4.22, server: 0.0.0.0:8443
```
sometimes we also see "no peer certificate presented" in app logs.

alex: that "wrong version number" often means something speaking plaintext to TLS port, or a proxy mangling bytes. NAT gateway only does TCP pass-through though. Are we using any egress proxies for the dedicated fleet?

maria: yes — for cost reasons some workloads go via our egress proxy cluster (envoy) in the same VPC. but the failing requests appear when that path is used. requests that go direct to ALB do not fail.

olivia: can we confirm whether the ALB is doing host-header based routing or ALB rule matching that picks a TLS cert? if the ALB picks default cert and then reoriginates with no SNI to backend, backends that require client SNI might reject.

jun: quick check: run `openssl s_client -connect alb-host:443 -servername model.redwood.ai` from a host in the failing NAT subnet and compare to a direct node. maybe the SNI isn't being forwarded on TLS re-origin.

maria: did that just now. curl from failing path shows TLS OK to ALB, but backend connection had empty SNI:
```
# on backend nginx (debug ssl): SNI: ''\n# client cert verify: failed - no peer cert
```

alex: sounds like ALB (classic application load balancer) when configured with HTTP->HTTPS or when doing TLS termination may not set SNI on the reorigin TLS connection unless you enable client-preserved SNI or supply certificate to target group. Not sure exact AWS behavior.

ops-bot: deploy: certificate-rotation-2026-03-18 started by @infra-bot :hourglass_flowing_sand:

maria: also worth noting: the failing pod IPs are in the 10.0.4.0/24 range which get SNATed to our egress nodes. egress nodes run an outbound envoy instance that rewrites the downstream TCP stream with PROXY v2 (we enabled for LB visibility). maybe proxy header is confusing the ALB when it expects raw TLS bytes.

jun: AH — if PROXY protocol v2 is injected between envoy and ALB (or to the backend) and the ALB or nginx isn't expecting it, the first bytes will be the PROXY header, which looks like binary and will lead to "wrong version number" on SSL. But why only on NAT path? because we enabled proxy protocol for that path to preserve client IP.

olivia: rollout of proxy protocol to egress was recent — that would match timing. Could also explain missing SNI if reorigin path reads header instead of TLS ClientHello.

maria: quick experiment: disabled proxy_protocol on the egress envoys for a single AZ and reran tests — failures disappeared for that AZ.

alex: nice, so two orthogonal problems: 1) PROXY header being prepended to TLS causing handshake error, 2) ALB/backends losing SNI on reorigin when a TLS-offloaded ALB is used. For (2) we should check ALB target group TLS settings: enable "Preserve SNI" (if available) or use TCP passthrough via NLB for end-to-end TLS so SNI reaches backend.

jun: long-term: prefer NLB with TLS passthrough for model traffic that requires client certs. short-term: disable proxy protocol for egress-to-alb connections or ensure proxy inserts PROXY header only for plaintext HTTP paths, not TLS-on-TLS.

maria: opened a short ticket with steps and a config diff. patching egress envoy config to not insert proxy proto v2 for ports 443 -> ALB.

olivia: schedule a canary to us-west-2 dedicated pool, update infra runbook, and check for other services that may be impacted by turning off proxy_proto. also check ALB listener -> target TLS SNI behavior and if we can set `ssl-parameters` or `preserve-client-sni` in terraform module.

maria: added canary run and smoke tests. will monitor next 30m and report. thanks all. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: incident-note: 1768123456 recorded - root cause suspected: PROXY protocol + ALB TLS reorigination causing client cert/SNI loss. mitigations: revert proxy-proto on egress and evaluate NLB passthrough for cert-validated routes."
